newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to announce bid for CEFTA membership.
newsitem.headline: Romania to announce bid for CEFTA membership.

text.p: Romania will officially launch its bid to join the Central European Free Trade Agreement at a CEFTA summit this week, Foreign Affairs spokesman Sorin Ducaru said on Wednesday.
Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu is expected to head the Romanian delegation at the meeting in the Slovakian city of Jasna.
"Romania is expected to present its decision to start negotiations to join CEFTA and become part of the accord starting January 1997," Ducaru told journalists.
Last month ministers from the five CEFTA countries said Romania and Bulgaria could be the next new members of the organisation provided they adjusted their agricultural policies.

CEFTA was formed in 1992 by Hungary, Poland and former Czechoslovakia as a European Union-type grouping to replace the communist-era trading bloc Comecon. It is currently made up of Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Slovenia.
Slovakia is currently president of the organisation.
Romania already has free-trade accords with the Czech Republic and Slovakia, while negotiations with Hungary, Poland and Slovenia are in an advance stage, Ducaru said.
Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and the Ukraine are also seeking CEFTA membership.
The CEFTA summit will deal with further liberalisation of mutual trade and coordination of efforts to gain entry to the European Union. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
